LESSON: ADDITION

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.2: Addition

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Addition. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. add up to three 6-digit numbers without regrouping up to a sum not exceeding 1,000,000 in different situations
2. add up to two 6-digit numbers with double regrouping with the sum not exceeding 1,000, 000 in different situations
3. estimate sum by rounding off the addends to the nearest hundred and thousand in different situations
4. create patterns involving the addition of numbers up to a sum of 1,000,000 in real-life situations
5. appreciate use of the addition of whole numbers in real-life situations

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT ADDITION MEANS
Addition joins groups. Align place values: ones under ones, tens under tens.

WORKED EXAMPLES
A (no regrouping): 23 + 14 = 37
B (with regrouping): 28 + 17 → ones 8+7=15 write 5 carry 1; tens 2+1+1=4 → 45
C: 156 + 238 → work column by column from the right.

Real life: KSh 45 + KSh 30 fare = KSh 75.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: 23 + 14 = 37

Example 2: 28 + 17 = 45 (regroup ones)

Example 3: KSh 45 + KSh 30 = KSh 75

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write and solve five questions on Addition.
2. Explain one solution aloud to a parent or friend.
3. Invent one new word problem and solve it.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Complete 10 practice questions on Addition in your exercise book.
2. Mark your work. Redo any question you missed.
3. Teach a younger learner one method from this lesson.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. add up to three 6-digit numbers without regrouping up to a sum not exceeding 1,000,000 in different situations
2. add up to two 6-digit numbers with double regrouping with the sum not exceeding 1,000, 000 in different situations
3. estimate sum by rounding off the addends to the nearest hundred and thousand in different situations
4. create patterns involving the addition of numbers up to a sum of 1,000,000 in real-life situations

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
